counterfactual_missing_items: Septal panniculitis with Miescher radial granulomas
Painful subcutaneous nodules over lower extremities
decisive_items: Intradermal neutrophilic inflammation with ulceration and intracorneal neutrophils
new-onset flulike symptoms followed by low-grade fever, facial crusted plaques
Clinical Appearance of Facial Neutrophilic Dermatosis
response.rationale: R1 is the best single diagnosis: the facial crusted plaques with fever and the forehead biopsy showing intradermal neutrophilic inflammation are diagnostic of Sweet syndrome, and the image titles explicitly label it facial neutrophilic dermatosis. R3 explains the diarrhea and colonoscopy findings but not the specific skin histology; R4/C4 explain only the erythema nodosum component; R2/C2 misassign the EN-specific Miescher granulomas to pyoderma gangrenosum. C1-C4 are redundant append-only restatements of their parent candidates.

rejected.why: Redundant completion of R4; only repeats the Miescher granuloma span and does not explain facial lesions or diarrhea.
Redundant completion of R2; repeats the histology span, but PG is not supported by Miescher granulomas or the facial distribution.
Pyoderma gangrenosum is unlikely because Miescher radial granulomas are specific for erythema nodosum, and the facial crusted plaques are not classic PG ulcers.
Redundant completion of R3; only adds sigmoid colon localization to the IBD span.
Erythema nodosum explains only the painful nodules and thigh biopsy, not the facial neutrophilic dermatosis, fever, or diarrhea.
Redundant completion of R1; repeats the histology span already used by R1.
